<thought>The proton NMR spectra show chemical shifts at 2.93 ppm (dd, 3H), 4.43 ppm (dd, 1H), 5.04 ppm (dd, 2H), and 6.05 ppm (ddd, 1H). The presence of doublets and doublet of doublets suggests coupling between protons, indicating a complex structure with possible alkenes or aromatic systems. The shift at 4.43 ppm could be indicative of a proton on a carbon adjacent to an electronegative atom, such as oxygen. The shifts at 5.04 ppm and 6.05 ppm suggest the presence of vinylic protons, which are common in alkenes. To further refine the structure, I will obtain the IR spectra to identify any functional groups present.</thought>

<thought>The IR spectra show peaks at 3541, 3132, 3099, 3082, 3047, 3039, 3003, 2818, and 1712 cm⁻¹. The peak at 3541 cm⁻¹ suggests the presence of an O-H group, likely an alcohol. The peaks around 3000 cm⁻¹ indicate C-H stretching in alkenes or aromatics. The peak at 1712 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a carbonyl group (C=O), suggesting the presence of a ketone or aldehyde. Given the NMR and IR data, the molecule likely contains an aromatic ring, an alcohol, and a carbonyl group. To further refine the structure, I will use the HSQC NMR spectra to correlate the carbon and proton environments.</thought>

<thought>The HSQC NMR spectra provide correlations between protons and their directly attached carbons. The correlations are as follows: 2.93 ppm with 43.7 ppm, 3.03 ppm with 54 ppm, 4.43 ppm with 70.5 ppm, 5.04 ppm and 5.11 ppm with 117.4 ppm, and 6.05 ppm with 135.8 ppm. This data supports the presence of an aromatic system (117.4 and 135.8 ppm) and an alcohol or ether (70.5 ppm). The carbonyl group indicated by the IR spectra (1712 cm⁻¹) is not directly observed in the HSQC, as it typically does not have directly attached protons. Given the data, the molecule likely contains an aromatic ring, an alcohol, and a carbonyl group. I will now attempt to deduce the SMILES string based on this information.</thought>
